newsitem.title: USA: Frigid cold to blanket central U.S. this week.
newsitem.headline: Frigid cold to blanket central U.S. this week.

text.p: Frigid cold will blanket the United States from the Rocky Mountains to the Appalachians this week with sub-zero temperatures extending deep into Texas, forecasters said.
The bone-chilling cold was forecast to last into next week which should drive up home heating costs and possibly slow oil refinery operations along the U.S. Gulf coast, they said.
"Natural gas usage in the Midwest will skyrocket," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Lows of minus 10 to minus 20 degrees Fahrenheit were forecast from the Dakotas to Nebraska and sub-zero into Texas.
The cold and accompanying wind may threaten unprotected livestock from North Dakota to Texas, forecasters said.
Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather, said the cold should gradually spread in the eastern and northern U.S., but largely miss the Florida orange growing region.
"At least for the next 10 days we don't see any threat to the Florida orange crop," Solberg said.
Snow from the system should largely remain in northern Iowa, Minnesota and the Dakotas, with accumulations of one to four inches a day through Wednesday, said WSC's Burgio.
A second cold front was forecast Christmas week which should produce similar temperatures over much of the same area, but may produce a greater amount of snow.
"We really don't see an end to it," said Solberg of the cold. "If we don't have a white Christmas, we certainly will have a cold one."
